question: A sphere is completely contained within a cylinder, with the height and diameter of the cylinder matching the diameter of the sphere. Given that the volume of the sphere is 36π cm³, what is the volume of the vacant space inside the cylinder?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The volume of a cylinder that completely circumscribes a sphere is exactly (3/2) times the volume of the sphere.

Ratio of Cylinder Volume to Sphere Volume = 3 : 2.

Vacant Space = Cylinder Volume − Sphere Volume = (3/2 − 1) = 1/2 of Sphere Volume.

Vacant Space = (1/2) × 36π = 18π cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 18π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume of the sphere = 36π cm³

Height and diameter of the cylinder = Diameter of the sphere

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Sphere = (4/3)πr³

Volume of Cylinder = πr²h
